data:
This course explores foundational and contemporary perspectives on personality, self, and
 identity in psychology. It asks the fundamental question: Who are we, and what makes us who
 we are? What makes us both unique and part of a shared social world? Beginning with classical
 debates on the nature and structure of personality, students are introduced to how psychology
 has historically conceptualized the individual. The course then moves into critical examinations
 of how selfhood is shaped by social, cultural, and digital environments, as well as by
 experiences of displacement and diaspora. Drawing from diverse psychological
 traditions—including trait theory, psychoanalysis, developmental psychology, and critical/cultural
 psychology—the course investigates how identities are formed, narrated, regulated, and
 transformed. Particular emphasis is placed on Indian psychological thought, contextual
 differences, and the lived experience of navigating multiple, intersecting selves.
